lots.what_it_is: Great Britain, Queen Victoria Jubilee coinage silver crown, 1891 (Spink 3921), 0.925 silver, 28.28 g standard weight (about 0.841 oz fine). Only the St George and dragon reverse is photographed. Gowans title: 1891 SILVER CROWN. It sits loose in a reused J.M. Crafts jewellery gift box whose label reads 'Set with Blue Lace Agate'. That label belongs to the box, not the coin.

sold.note: SOLD, same_item: close. Page opened (curl). 'Queen Victoria, Jubilee coinage, crown, 1889 (S.3921). Cleaned, otherwise nearly extremely fine.' Estimate $100. Same design and weight, but a different date: 1889 had a much bigger mintage, so it is commoner than 1891. Better grade than this lot but cleaned. The page does not say whether the figure includes Noble's buyer's premium; I treat it as hammer. No conversion (AUD).

SOLD, same_item: close. Page opened (curl). 1889 Jubilee crown, 'Cleaned extremely fine/good extremely fine', estimate $100. Commoner date and a clearly better grade than this worn coin, so it is an upper marker. Premium basis not stated.

SOLD, same_item: close (group lot). Page opened (curl). Contents: an 1891 crown (S.3921) in Very Good, a 1797 cartwheel twopence (Very Good) and a very worn Roman bronze. The crown is the same date and in similar or slightly lower grade than this lot. Part of the $120 belongs to the cartwheel twopence, so the crown's own share is perhaps $60 to $90 (my estimate). It cannot set a bid on its own. Premium basis not stated.

unsold.note: UNSOLD, same_item: close (same date, much better grade). Page opened (curl). 1891 crown, 'Grey toned, nearly extremely fine/extremely fine', estimate $200, passed in. A ceiling signal for a far better coin, and older than 24 months.

lots.guide_summary: AUD 80 to 200, all AUD so no conversion. Sold: 3 Noble results, all close rather than exact. Two are single 1889 crowns in cleaned nEF/EF at $80 and $130 (Mar 2025). The third is a group of 3 including an 1891 crown in VG, $120 (Jul 2025). Unsold: an 1891 crown in nEF/EF passed in at a $200 estimate (Apr 2024). Asking: none. Category guide only, not in the range: Noble Sale 141 (Apr 2026) lot 1215, 1887 crown EF with a lamination flaw, sold $100 (https://www.noble.com.au/auctions/lot/?id=439974, page opened). For a worn Fine-ish 1891 crown, realistic auction value is about silver value plus a little: roughly $70 to $110 hammer.
lots.working: No SOLD entry is the same item in similar condition: no single 1891 crown in about Fine sold within 24 months. The single sales are 1889 crowns in better (cleaned) grades, and the only 1891 sale is bundled with other coins. So under the rules keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. For reference only, not a bid limit: if you treated the cleaned 1889 nEF at $80 as the comparable, $80 / 1.198 = 66.8, rounded down to $65 hammer ($77.87 all-in). Melt: 0.841 oz fine x AUD 84.67 Perth Mint spot bid = about $71, which is a $59 hammer at break-even ($71 / 1.198). At the Perth Mint buy rate for sub-99.9 silver (AUD 69.43 per fine oz) it is $58. Both rates are from https://www.perthmint.com/invest/information-for-investors/metal-prices, page opened, updated 07/10/2026 10:00 PM. There is no flip margin: resale of about $80 to $100, less about 13% fees and $10 postage, gives about $60 to $77, and dividing by 2.396 gives a hammer of $25 to $30. The lot already shows 5 bids (no current bid figure in the saved page). Pickup from 37 Main Road, Moonah, inbound freight $0. The researcher's search budget was used up. Mine was too (WebSearch refused), so all evidence came from Noble's own archive search pages, opened directly.
lots.confidence_reason: Only the reverse is photographed, so the obverse (holes, graffiti, mount marks, damage) and the edge are unseen. The date is read clearly but the grade is judged from one photo. No exact same-item single SOLD result in the last 24 months.
lots.dropped_entries: Researcher supplied no entries. Considered and dropped: Noble Sale 142 lot 951 (1890 crown with three other coins, $260) and lot 963 (1891 crown with 33 pennies and a shilling, $220), because both are groups where the other coins carry much of the price. Noble Sale 117 lot 1872 (1891 crown nUNC, $260) is years old and a far better grade.
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo, reverse only: Pistrucci St George and the dragon, date 1891 clear in the exergue. Even wear on the horse's musculature, St George's cloak and the dragon, with light grey toning and small contact marks. I would call it about Fine, possibly gF. Rim looks intact in this view, with no visible hole or solder on the reverse. The coin sits loose on velvet in a J.M. Crafts jewellery box labelled 'Set with Blue Lace Agate'. The box is a reused gift box and says nothing about the coin. Lot sticker reads 138.
lots.condition: Circulated, about Fine (from reverse only), toned. Obverse and edge not seen.
lots.question_for_gowans: Please can you describe or photograph the obverse and edge of lot 138 (1891 crown)? Is there any hole, mount or solder mark, graffiti, bending or cleaning? And can you confirm the weight is about 28 g?

lots.what_it_is: Two sheets of Australian pre-decimal coins (Gowans title: 2 SHEETS OF PRE-DECIMAL CURRENCY INCL SILVER). Sheet 1 holds 20 carded silver coins with dealer pencil prices of $2 to $12 (total $90). Threepences: 1936, 1950, 1955, 1963. Sixpences: 1942D x2, 1945 x2, 1946, 1951PL, 1955, 1957, 1960, 1962 x2, 1963. Shillings: 1954, 1961. Florins: 1951, 1962. Sheet 2 holds 42 bronze pennies (6 x 7 pockets). The researcher said about 80 pennies and halfpennies, but I count 42 and all look like pennies. Readable dates include 1919, 1920, 1924, 1927 (x2+), 1933, 1935, 1949, 1952, 1956 and 1964. Several are unreadable through the plastic, and one is hidden under the lot sticker.

sold.note: SOLD, same_item: category guide. Page opened (curl). 119 pennies; threepences (16), sixpences (20), shillings (7) and florins (15), with fineness listed. Fine to unc. I estimate its silver at about 5.6 oz fine against about 1.35 oz in this lot, so scaled by silver it implies about $130 for this lot. Bigger and better lot. Premium basis not stated.

SOLD, same_item: category guide. Page opened (curl). 1919-1964 florins (12), shillings (16), sixpences (21), threepences (21), and about 60 pennies and halfpennies. Fine to EF. At least about 5 oz fine silver, so scaled to this lot's silver it implies about $80. Premium basis not stated.

lots.guide_summary: AUD 80 to 135, but only as a scaled category guide, not same-item evidence. Sold: 2 Noble bulk pre-decimal lots (Apr and Jul 2026), scaled down by silver content. Unsold: none. Asking: none (the $90 total of the dealer's pencil prices on the cards is a retail ask, not filed as an entry). Melt floor about $94 to $115 (see working). All AUD, no conversion.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD evidence (an odd mixed lot is never the same item), so both maximums are 0. Silver content from standard weights (3d 1.41 g, 6d 2.82 g, 1/- 5.65 g, 2/- 11.31 g). At 0.925: the 1936 3d and four sixpences (1942D x2, 1945 x2), 11.7 g fine. At 0.500: 3d x3, 6d x8, 1/- x2 and 2/- x2, 30.4 g fine. Total about 42.1 g, or 1.353 oz fine. At AUD 84.67 Perth Mint spot bid that is about $115. At the Perth Mint buy rate for sub-99.9 silver (AUD 69.43 per fine oz) it is about $94. Source: https://www.perthmint.com/invest/information-for-investors/metal-prices, page opened, updated 07/10/2026 10:00 PM. For reference only, not a bid: the scrap break-even hammer is about $94 / 1.198 = $78. Common circulated pennies add little, perhaps $10 to $20 (unverified). Pickup Moonah, inbound freight $0. The current bid figure is not in the saved page (1 bid recorded). WebSearch was unavailable (shared budget used up), so the evidence came from Noble's own archive search.
lots.confidence_reason: The evidence is scaled category-guide sales only. Several penny dates are unreadable, including the one under the lot sticker. Coin grades are judged from photos.
lots.dropped_entries: Researcher supplied no entries. Considered and dropped: Noble Sale 142 lot 20 ($240), which is mostly EF-unc with 15 florins, a much heavier and better lot. Noble Sale 139 lots 765/769/772/774 ($400 to $1,800) are large albums with key dates, not comparable.
lots.key_photo_findings: Silver sheet: 20 coins in 2x2 card holders with handwritten dates and pencil prices. Pre-1946 0.925 coins: 1936 threepence, 1942D sixpence x2, 1945 sixpence x2. The rest are 0.500 silver from 1946 to 1963. Grades look Fine to VF. The florins (1951 standard arms, 1962) are the heaviest silver. Penny sheet: 42 pennies of both the Commonwealth 'ONE PENNY' type (1919-1936) and the kangaroo type (1938-1964), mostly worn browns. I could not see an obvious 1925, 1930 or 1946 key date, but about 8 dates are unreadable and one is under the sticker. The researcher's '80 pennies and halfpennies' is wrong: there are 42 pennies.
lots.condition: Circulated, mostly Fine to VF. Common dates as far as can be read.
lots.question_for_gowans: For lot 159, could you tell me the date of the penny under the lot sticker and of any pennies whose dates can't be read through the sleeve? Is there a 1925, 1930 or 1946 among them? Also, are there exactly 20 silver coins and 42 pennies?

lots.what_it_is: Moorcroft small squat baluster vase on a short foot, tube-lined Orchid pattern (pink, red, yellow and purple orchids with green leaves) on a dark cobalt ground, 7.5 cm (Gowans: MOORCROFT VASE - ORCHID PATTERN - 1/7.5CM). The base has a blurred blue MOORCROFT mark in capitals, with a blue smudge above it and a blue painted streak (probably initials) at lower right. This fits the Walter Moorcroft period, roughly 1950s to 1980s. It is not the earlier W. Moorcroft script signature.
lots.guide_summary: No evidence survives: no sold, unsold or asking entries. The researcher found none, and my WebSearch calls were refused (shared budget used up). Direct tries failed: an Invaluable Moorcroft artist page (ID unknown, generic page returned), LiveAuctioneers (script-only page), and the Leonard Joel, Lawsons, Theodore Bruce and Gibson's site searches (no lot data). The blind $80 to $150 estimate remains unverified.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. If evidence were found, all-in = hammer x 1.198 (Gowans 19.8%). Pickup Moonah, inbound freight $0. 0 bids at the 07/10/2026 check.
lots.confidence_reason: There is no market evidence. The base mark is smeared and only partly legible. The base shows a crack-like line that could be a hairline in the body or a firing flaw, which would cut the value sharply.
lots.dropped_entries: Researcher supplied no entries, and none were added.
lots.key_photo_findings: Side view: bright tube-lined orchids, glossy cobalt ground, fine crazing in the coloured glazes. No chips visible on the rim or body from this one side. Base (enlarged): fully crazed cream glaze. A blue MOORCROFT mark, heavily blurred where the blue ran in firing. A blue streak at lower right that is probably the painted WM initials. A green dab near the foot rim. Most important: a distinct dark irregular line runs from near the centre of the base towards the right. It is wider and darker than the crazing, so it may be a hairline crack or a firing crack in the base. The foot rim shows dirt and flecks of blue glaze.
lots.condition: Body looks good from one side. Possible hairline or firing crack across the base. Overall crazing. Mark blurred.
lots.question_for_gowans: For lot 195, the Moorcroft orchid vase: does the line across the base go right through? Does the vase ring true when tapped, and does the line show on the inside or the outside wall? Are there any chips, restoration or crazing stains on the side not photographed?
